proposals: The Central Pollution Control Board should publish annual data from its waste-tyre EPR portal: certificates generated by recycler and by end use — crumb rubber, retreading, pyrolysis — so that how much of the obligation is met through road-grade crumb rubber rather than informal pyrolysis can be checked.

The Central Pollution Control Board should publish an official annual estimate of waste-tyre generation and of the volume going to dumping, stockpiling or informal pyrolysis, so that the 1.5 million and 1 million tonne figures can be traced to a regulator rather than secondary sources.

NHAI and NRRDA should report each year the kilometres of road laid with crumb-rubber modified bitumen and the tonnes of crumb rubber used, so that the shift from trial sections to mainstream use can be measured against the bitumen import bill.

The Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell should report bitumen consumption split between plain, crumb-rubber modified and polymer-modified grades, so that the share of India's 8.8 million tonnes of bitumen demand already met with modified binders is known.
